recorded: 2026-09-29, gfx1151 Strix Halo (zbook, AMD Radeon 8060S, 126976 MiB), Gemma 4 26B-A4B, UD-Q4_K_XL, gfx1151 build
why: The campaign metric has been a 512-token prefill for roughly three hundred iterations, so the objective's actual complaint -- prefill far below llama.cpp -- had never been measured where it is worst. The same-host llama.cpp reference is flat across the ladder (1012.98, 1057.48, 1067.14, 1039.85 tok/s at pp512/1024/2048/4096) while this engine's own old gfx1151 numbers fell (271, 251, 220). This records the current ladder at the reference's protocol and attributes the shape of the remaining gap to a named kernel.

reference.reading: flat within 3 percent across an eightfold prompt range

engine_ladder.command:
env -u HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES PYTHONPATH=. HIPENGINE_HIP_ARCH=gfx1151 .venv/bin/python scripts/gemma4_campaign_bench.py --prompt

--output 128 --samples 3 --warmup 1 --expect-gpu 8060S --label ladder --out /tmp/ladder_

.json
engine_ladder.protocol: same token ids as the llama.cpp reference protocol; fixed-length rows, EOS ignored; three samples per point, spread under 1 percent at every point; path parity True in every run
engine_ladder.reading: the engine's prefill rate falls 870 -> 454 tok/s across an eightfold prompt range, 2.47x per doubling, while the reference is flat. The gap is therefore not a constant factor to shave: it widens with prompt length, and the objective's long-prompt cases are the worst case.

attribution.instrument: scripts/gemma4_prefill_kernel_census.py, HIP event pairs around every kernel wrapper the decoder layer calls, recorded per call and synchronised once at the end
attribution.accounting: 98.5 percent at 512, 98.9 percent at 2048, 98.9 percent at 4096
attribution.note: the prefill is chunked at max_block 512, so a 4096-token prompt issues 8 chunks x 30 layers = 240 attention calls
attribution.finding: every non-attention term scales linearly -- 7.4 to 7.8x for 8x the tokens, the same shape as the reference. Attention is the only superlinear term at 41.13x for 8x the tokens, and at 4096 tokens it is 61.0 percent of the step. The non-attention total at 4096 is 3534 ms against the reference's entire 4096-token prefill of about 3940 ms, so the whole remaining gap is the attention kernel.
attribution.attention_rate: the 4096-token prefill performs 1524.7 GFLOP of attention in 5.5207 s, 276 GFLOP/s, on the order of one percent of this part's bf16 rate. The rate is flat in length -- 2026-09-28-gemma4-gfx1151-prefill-attention-length-scaling.json measured 426.9, 452.2 and 421.2 GFLOP/s on the sliding layers at 512, 1024 and 2048 -- so there is no length-dependent inefficiency to remove: the kernel is slow at every length and its share grows because it is the only quadratic term.
attribution.structure: hipengine/kernels/hip_gfx1100/gemma4/gemma4_attention.hip launches one block of 256 threads per (token, head) and walks the keys three times -- logits into a shared array, a block max and denominator, then a weighted sum over V. There is no query tiling, so every K/V row is re-read once per query token, and the per-key loop is scalar. 20260929T073000 measured the K/V load and its dot at 25 percent of the kernel and the surrounding per-key machinery -- mask test, LDS write, block max, softmax rescale, loop scalars -- at 75 percent.

not_a_promotion: This row measures the current default. It promotes nothing, changes no default, and is not a hipEngine claim against a prior hipEngine row.
